items.note: Samarāṅgaṇasūtradhāra prescription on the sthapati: must know both śāstra and practice; the king should punish one who poses as sthapati without śāstra.
items.gloss: One who becomes a practising sthapati without knowing the shastra, the king himself should kill, for he is a very death for the king; one who knows only shastra and is not skilled in practice loses his senses when work comes, like a coward in battle; one who knows only practice but not shastra is like a helpless blind man led along paths by another.

items.note: The sthapati's required character (śīla) and eight kinds of work (drawing, writing, woodwork, construction, stone work, gold work, mechanical/play art, craftsmanship).
items.gloss: A craftsman, though knowing, eloquent and devoted to work, is not good if without character; the virtuous is honoured in society; so the sthapati should take special care of character; the sthapati must always know eight kinds of work - aalekha (drawing), writing, wood-work, chaya (material, building, door, rampart etc.), accomplishment in stone work, gold work, mechanical or play art, and craftsmanship; knowing these he is honoured in the assembly of artisans.
